txt: *I* think we should eat it. If it's a leaf you can put it in your mouth. Or a reed. Yum yum.
...be together. You open your eyes and it's still there -- a giant stick insect, spinning slowly -- its limbs long and slender....

...hissing and clicking, it extends its mandible-like antennae to greet you. You're right below it now, looking up at the colossal chitin of its white limbs. The head of the creature is crowned by reeds and its eyes are like small droplets of water.
...phasmid! You open your eyes and there still is, spinning slowly -- in absolute  silence -- its limbs long and slender...
A delicate tangle of arms and legs unfolds from the reeds, limb by limb -- to then just stand there, moving its scythe-like arms in ghostly silence.
A series of chirrups surrounds you, like swallows on a cliff side, as the phasmid moves its forearms -- tymbals visible on the inside of its white stalks...

A shudder pulses through the creatures limbs. It jolts back to life, like a record continuing were it left off -- in a swaying, praying motion. Even the small black pearls of its eyes do not stray from you...
A small shudder passes the creature's arm. High above you its black pearl-eyes still glisten, mesmerized by the light passing its nervous system.
A sudden chirrup fills the air -- the walking stick moves its whole body, limbs working independently of each other, like the parts of a masterfully constructed machine.
A sudden shiver passes the limb. Looks like the creature is awakening, wave by wave from its stupor.
Also very, very dangerous.
And just like that it's gone -- skating away across the sea's calm mirror like a skipping stone, leaving nothing but  circles on the water...

And when you fall we will come to raise you up, bud from you, banner-like, blossom from you and carry you apart in a sky funeral. In honour of your passing. (But not me, because I am just a leaf eater.)
Another shudder passes through the forearm under your palm -- feels like blood pumping through a brain. It's coming to, you withdraw your hand slowly.

Another shudder pulses through the creatures limbs. It jolts back to life, like a record continuing were it left off -- in a swaying, praying motion. Even the small black pearls of its eyes do not stray from you...
Are you sure?
As you do, the invertebrate comes to life, its limbs moving independent of each other. As if each has a mind of its own. They are white like stalks of porcelain, knitting above you.
As you're turning away, the phasmid mirrors your movements, stepping on the water -- the long limbs carry its feather weight without breaking its surface.
Back on an island 28 kilometres away, the gigantic insect moves its antennae, taking its measure of the air, slowly... it's searching for something -- *you*.
But you *can*. You open your eyes and it's still there -- a giant stick insect, spinning slowly -- -- its limbs long and slender...
Even when you're sleeping... And when you wake, you carry it around on your neck. With eyes open that cannot help but swallow more behind the mirror. I feel great, mute empathy for you.
Everything your eyes touch goes back there -- behind the nerve mirror. What if you blink? Are we still here? (Please don't blink). What if you misplace us all one day -- or just forget?

Few of us can begin to imagine the horror of you -- with all of creation reflected in your forebrain. It must be like the highest of hells, a kaleidoscope of fire and writhing glass. Eternal damnation.
Fire? Where?
For me it is a series of half-lit images. A kind of darkness, being intruded upon. Transient. Dim. Moist.
For me it is not like that. I have states, not emotions. For example, I experience excitement at unexpected sugar rewards, but that is not important.
From the corner of your eye, you see a sudden cascade of motion ripple through the insect's limbs. A series of ultrasonic clicks fills your ear...
Good bye. A series of chirrups surrounds you, like swallows on a cliff side, as the phasmid moves its forearms -- tymbals visible on the inside of its white stalks...
He is in a bad state, deteriorating fast now. He thinks I am beneficial to him, but I am not. I only quicken his deterioration.
He not as much as glances at the gigantic insect to his right -- nor does it look at him. Its antennae take their measure of the air, slowly... searching for something -- *you*.

Hissing and clicking, the arthropod extends its mandible-like antennae to greet you again. You're right below it, looking up at the colossal chitin of its white limbs. Its small eyes look at nothing in particular.
I already did.

I am an unknown species of the order Phantasmodea -- endemic to the Insulindian isola. For the last three hundred and fifty years I have hidden in plain sight, masquerading as the reeds. Moulding, cloning myself, unfolding at night to play with trash bins and buoys.
I am at the end of a narrow funnel. Weightless. So light it only feels like *something* to be me. In truth -- perhaps I'm nothing? I certainly do not have a soul. And if I did, it would never ache.
I am not. There isn't even a central nervous system in my head. Only mouthparts for eating wetland plants.
I am oblivious to the city. It is only on my margins. A ball I sometimes spin. A toy, Or the cylinder of a discarded trash bin.
I can also detect pheromones -- the ones on you tell me that you will not eat me. And that I will benefit from your closeness. In short, I love you.
I do not have fire inside me. In me there is not even blood, but lymph -- like sap from a wine palm.
I don't know. You're just a shadow for me. Far away, faintly transmitting, but for a curious smell.
I exist.

I have stayed hidden through four forms of government and two scientific revolutions. Until I was accidentally discovered by a detective of the Citizens Militia in Revachol, district of Martinaise, March, '51.
I smelled it, as soon as you stepped on the island -- strawberries. Fresh burst of red strawberries. Ripe turning riper. Soon you will be rotten.

I went unnoticed by the first settlers and the land surveyors of the suzerain. Also by the soldiers of the Revolution and the officials of the occupation. Even the Semenese islanders who came here first, but did not stay, have not seen me.
It doesn't look like that.
It is a nervous shadow cast into the world by you, eating away at reality. A great, unnatural territory. Its advent coincides with the arrival of the human mind.
It is impossible to see inside. There is only chitin, pretending to be reeds -- or polished, like stalks of marble. The occasional series of clicks, undecipherable to the human ear.
It's really there. Spinning slowly -- in absolute silence -- its limbs long and slender.
It's really there. Spinning slowly -- in absolute silence -- its limbs long and slender...
It's spread too thin among its limbs, performing incomprehensible operations on the world; and you -- looking at it, mouth slightly open... You cannot even imagine what it thinks.
It's still there -- an unfolding mechanism of reed-like chitin. Hovering in place.
Mute, the insect foams from its mouthparts, tilting the plates of its fused together head. From left to right, without reason.
No -- you're only thinking it *now*. This is a revelation.
No one believed I exist -- almost no one. Until you came, detective. Dripping of blood that smells like strawberries. Across the calm sea, the first in a thousand years.
No one would. You open your eyes and it's still there -- a giant stick insect, spinning slowly -- its limbs long and slender. Silent as death...
No reply. A total, ancient silence comes from its mouth, along with what appears to be some kind of foam... The stridulations of its limbs continue all around you.
No. *You* are. The moral of our encounter is: I am a relatively median lifeform -- while it is you who are total, extreme madness. A volatile simian nervous system, ominously new to the planet.
No. No one believed I exist -- almost no one. Until you came, detective. Dripping of blood that smells like strawberries.  Across the calm sea, the first in a thousand years.
No. The leg tried to move around independently, making it hard to walk.
No. There is *one* more.
No. You are awake. I am real. Light is forming me. This is real.
No. You are the miracle.
Not even the birds know that. Not even the water lilies.

Nothing changes in the cyclical, praying motion of the creature's limbs. They are porcelain white on the inside, and reed-coloured on the out -- beige, light brown and striped. You are unsure if it is scared or not.
Now I will tell you how it is for me. For me it is a series of half-lit images. A kind of darkness, being intruded upon. Transient. Dim. Moist.
Now I will tell you what it's like for me. For me it is a series of half-lit images. A kind of darkness, being intruded upon. Transient. Dim. Moist.
Of course, it is nothing compared to the horror that is you -- with all of creation reflected in your forebrain, in terrible fidelity, a fire mirror. Eternal, never-ending damnation.
Please be. Or one day one of you will close your eyes and sigh -- and open them to see that none of this ever existed.
Please do not do that again.
Reed-like tufts stick out of its joints. As the insect moves its forearms it produces a faint hiss -- like a reel-to-reel machine spinning after the tape breaks.
Sets of complex eyes follow you --droplets of dew on either side of the head.
Shapes of plants and animals. And *internal* sensations. A swarm of sounds, tiny vibrations on the inside of my forearms -- all speak of complexities totally beyond my understanding.
She was hell on Earth. It doesn't take a three-metre stick insect to tell you that.
She was middle class. It doesn't take a three-metre stick insect to tell you that.

Silence. Click. The foam slowly turns a darker tone, like burnt caramel -- as the insect moves its mouthparts, masticating on nothing in particular. Then the little bubbles begin to burst, one by one...
Simian butcherer... Soon, one of you will close your eyes -- and open them to see that none of this ever existed.
So am I. I was born to detect sucrose rewards and semiochemicals. What were you born to detect?
So it is *already* happening. One day, one of you will close your eyes and sigh -- and open them to see that none of this ever existed.
So it is already happening. Soon, one of you will close your eyes -- and open them to see that none of this ever existed.
So, you see, it's sometimes also difficult being a stick insect. The leg tried to move independently, making it hard to walk. But hearing about it makes you uncomfortable, I understand.
So, you see, it's sometimes difficult to be an insect. All of nature is a kind of horror, or strife -- though none of it as horrible as you. With all of creation reflected in your forebrain.
Sometimes, when moulting, I regrow a lost limb. One time something went wrong and a small leg replaced a missing antenna.
Spinning in silence -- limbs and antennae, like hair.
Tell me what it's like for you.
Thank you. I also have one final thing to say to you: that woman -- turn from the ruin. Turn and go *forward*.
That is your problem. Nothing ever ends for me. There is only room for two, maybe three pictures in my mind.

That must be incredibly hard. The arthropods are in silent and meaningless awe of you. Know that we are watching -- when you're tired, when the vision spins out of control. The insects will be looking on. Rooting for you.

The antennae hang from a great height. With your hand shaking you barely touch the tip of the left whisker. On contact the chitin curls into a spiral, like the tip of a poison ivy. Its touch on your fingertip feels cold, ticklish...
The arthropod follows you with its antennae. As you back off, the cracks and hisses of the tape that's come to its end grow more distant...

The arthropod towers above you -- just like in the picture -- oblivious to your chattering. The ventricles on its abdomen slowly expanding, vestigial wings like barely visible gossamer hanging from the inside of its slender joints.
The arthropod towers above you, frozen in place. A twitch passes one of its hind legs, as you...
The creature appears to have forgiven your nerves -- for now. There it still stands, a thin ghost on stilt-like legs. Antennae hang from its head, like curled strands of human hair.
The creature stands on long stilt-like legs, antennae hanging from its head like a woman's hair -- white and curled at the tips. It is no more than five steps away from you.
The creature tilts its tiny head to the side and appears to look at you. It is incredibly light, like the slightest gust of wind should blow it away, but it doesn't...
The foam slowly turns a darker shade, like burnt caramel -- as the insect moves its mouthparts, masticating. The little bubbles begin to burst, one by one...
The ghost insect watches you disengage, continuing its hypnotizing motion. It's unclear whether it even registers that you're going...
The insect stops its stridulation, seeming to observe you. Below its crown of reeds, little pin-prick eyes detect motion, glittering. The world stands still around you.
The insect's head is crowned with reed-like scales, the shape of seed heads. They rustle as the air moves. The ventricles at its abdomen continue to expanding, like lunglets...
The invertebrate comes back to life, stridulating. Sets of complex eyes follow you, moving in tandem, on either side of the insect's small head.

The invertebrate stops, raising its scythe-like arms and tilting its tiny head, formed from the fused plates around its mouth. For a second, the effigy is frozen, then it nudges back into motion with a click.
The leg tried to move around independently, making it hard to walk.
The limb before you is incredibly light, like eggshell. It's much lighter than a reed. You feel a soft push could tip the creature over, its hollow exoskeleton collapsing...
The moral of our encounter is: I am a relatively median lifeform, while you are extreme, all-engulfing madness. A volatile simian nervous system, ominously new to the planet.

The pale, too, came with you. No one remembers it before you. The cnidarians do not, the radially symmetricals do not. There is an almost unanimous agreement between the birds and the plants that you are going to destroy us all.
The reed-creature does not stop its stridulations -- it towers above you, parting the reeds it emerged from. Tuft like structures still rustle on its joints.

The shrill flash of the camera cuts the air like the blade of a sword. The phasmid freezes in its bright light -- head turned toward the lieutenant. Hypnotized by the flash, it stands frozen before you.
The spindly mechanism turns itself back to you, its antennae taking their measure of the air, slowly...
The stick insect is over three metres tall. It looks straight at you with its tiny pinprick eyes and its grotesquely small head.
Then I will tell you what it's like for me.
There is no change in the insects motion while its being aimed by the camera. It remains fixated on you.
There is no mind to speak of. And if there is, it's beyond your imagination -- too simple to be compatible with yours. Segmented mouthparts foam, it tilts its head.
There is only the old man -- and the giant stick insect spinning slowly -- in absolute silence -- it's long and thin limbs...
Unwittingly the insect continues its stridulations. As it moves, tuft-like structures still pretending to be plants rustle along on its joints.
Very slowly -- and only because he won't go away. It is meant to keep them from noticing me, to interfere with the pictures in their heads. But he has looked at me too long. And I'm destroying him.
Way too high. You open your eyes and it's still there -- a giant stick insect, spinning slowly -- its limbs long and slender. Silent as death...
We suspect it will be something like the oxygen holocaust that wiped out anaerobic life 2.6 billion years ago -- when organisms first started breathing. Only much worse.
What if it's not you? What if the three metres tall stick insect is having the vision -- while you're alone and  petrified.
What is your illness?

Yes -- with stone tools and silk. They too missed me, although I had not developed the mutation needed for parthenogenesis yet, and scoured the neolithic hinterland as distinct individuals, not clones.
Yes, I am lucky. It is nothing compared to the horror that is you -- with all of creation reflected in your forebrain. A nerve mirror of horrifying fidelity. Constant, never-ending damnation.
Yes, compared to the immeasurable, fiery empyrean of glass and terror in *your* head, it seems trivial. I just thought you should know.
Yes, holy is the lord of hosts. And all the Earth is filled with his glory.
Yes, thankfully someone ate it. The next time I moulted I grew an antenna again!
Yes. For me everything is *always* normal. God is in his heaven -- everything is normal on Earth.
Yes. I do not have a startle display, so I use a neurodegenerative allomone to aid in camouflage. Do not worry, it is only destructive over long periods of time.
Yes. I once cloned myself and ate the little ones. It was winter and I woke up at the wrong time. It was an accident.
Yes. No one detected me for such a long, long time. For thousands of years. I dithered, out of sight. Draped myself in greenery.
Yes. The leg tried to move around independently, making it hard to walk.
Yes. They don't mind.

You are a violent and irrepressible miracle. The vacuum of cosmos and the stars burning in it are afraid of you. Given enough time you would wipe us all out and replace us with nothing -- just by accident.
You can also eat it. If it's a leaf you can put it in your mouth. Yum yum. Or a reed.
You cannot lie to me. Behind you it smells of fires. So awfully far you were prepared to go in her presence. End it.
You see the insect turn to him, its mandible antennae reaching out. Its motions are quick, sudden.
You want to be a phasmid? Are you sure?
You were right. Little bubbles form on the mouthparts of the creature -- on its segmented lower lip. It looks to be foaming, slowly. The foam is white, then yellowish...
You're staring at me. For about three minutes now.
